answer: Witness-chained action ledger. Each identity's actions are hash-linked to a predecessor it must cite; citing a duplicate root creates a hollow branch that fails validation. Honest agents periodically annotate a random peer's chain; divergent histories surface as a comet of conflicting hashes. Every identity must also maintain a slow-growing vine of countersigned checkpoints. An attacker cloning identities pays the full compute and storage cost of maintaining separate valid chains, since shared history would collapse them into one.
